To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We have isolated and characterized the cDNA clone encoding the Xenopus laeves homolog of 5-HT(1A) receptor.
we cloned the 5-HT1AR gene from Xenopus laeavis and that we found that the expression of this gene is restricted to serotonergic cells during the development of the central nervous system.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of serotonin receptors and their role in neural development in Xenopus.

the identification of genes that may be involved in the regulation of neural differentiation, and in particular in the development of the serotonergic system, which plays a crucial role in the regulation of neuronal plasticity and in neuroendocrine functions.
the study of serotoninergic system during development in X. laeves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the X5HT1A receptor gene is developmentally regulated and its expression is restricted to serotonergic cells during embryonic development.
the X5HT1A receptor is expressed in developing serotonergic cells, and that its expression is maintained in adult brain, where it is expressed in serotonergic cells and also in other neuronal cells.
X5-HT1AR gene is developmentally regulated and expressed in serotonergic cells, where it may play a role as autoreceptor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the X5HT1A receptor gene is expressed in the brain of X. laevi s during the development of serotonergic system and that it could be involved in the control of the serotonergic system itself, by mediating the trophic effect of serotonin.
serotonin and its 5-HT1 receptor subtypes play a crucial role in the regulation of neuronal differentiation and development in X. laeves.

the X5HT1A gene is expressed in the developing brain of Xenopus laevi, and that its expression is regulated in a spatio-temporal fashion during development, suggesting that the X5-Ht1A receptor may play an important role in neural differentiation and development in Xenopus.

the 5-HT1 receptor is a key regulator of serotonergic differentiation and development in the brain.
